newsitem.title: UK: Analysts tend to lower gold price forecasts - poll.
newsitem.headline: Analysts tend to lower gold price forecasts - poll.

text.p: A drop in the gold price of 3-1/4 percent at the start of 1997 and the spectre of new bullion sales by central banks have led several analysts to revise down predictions for the value of the metal.

Reuters polled 13 analysts on January 9 and January 13 on their views for the spot gold price at the end of January and at the end of the first 1997. Most had lower end-quarter forecasts from those made in a similar poll in mid-December.

Only two of those who had been polled in December left their forecasts unchanged. And respondents taking part in the poll for the first time mostly saw prices lower at the end of January and at the end of the quarter than they are now.
The deepest downward revision was from Hanspeter Hausheer of Swiss Bank Corporation who downgraded the end-quarter figure to $350 from $375.
Gold fixed on Tuesday at $357.30 per ounce.
Hausheer cited confirmation of rumours of recent central bank selling of gold - by the Dutch central bank in a statement on Monday - as a reason behind his more bearish stance.
"Previously I thought it was just rumours that there had been selling from a European central bank. Now it seems that at least one has been active in the market selling," he said.
"It was not a problem to absorb the gold but now that one has done it, other banks could do it too."
Rhona O'Connell, a partner at stockbroker T. Hoare and Co cut her end-quarter forecast to $375 from $390.
"Overhead pressure is easing, judging by movements in lease rates, so there is no need for aggressive short covering," she said.
Analysts Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland and Jason Wong of Hong Kong's Po Sang Bank Ltd left forecasts unchanged.
Smith said, "Gold is an oversold market and the options ratchet effect on prices could take it higher more quickly than people think." He forecast an end=quarter price of $390.00.
Wong expected sentiment to remain weak discouraging people from buying gold and holding the price to $360 by April.
"The market will stay at this level, sticking to the lower end of the range as sentiment is quite bad. People are worried about sales from central banks," he said.
South African market analysts had mixed views. Angus Auchterlonie of Mathison and Hollidge saw prices rising with an end-January quote of $375 and an end-quarter value of $380.
"Fundamentally it should be a lot higher but I think we are still going to see overhanging jitters of the European Union and central banks selling," he said.
Dave Giese of Davis, Borkhum and Hare, and Nick Goodwin at Fedsure Asset Management were less bullish.

Giese forecast prices at end-January of $357 and at end-quarter of $360. "There is strong support level at $350 and quite a bit of resistance above $360. I think we are going to be dancing between $350 and $362," he said.
Goodwin saw prices sliding to $350 by the end of the month and $340 by the end of March. "I think it is going to be lower. There is ongoing pressure from central banks," he said.

Simon Middleton, gold analyst for the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE), forecast a modest jump to $365 by the end of the month and $374 by the end of the quarter - $6 less than he expected a month ago.

Two Japanese traders polled said spot gold may head lower as the bearish mood continues and the U.S. stock market climbs. Nobufumi Iimori, manager of Nihon Unicom Corporation, forecast $350 for Jauary and $342.50-$345.00 for the quarter.

Keiji Philip Yanagida, dealer of Mitsubishi Corporation saw gold at $350 at both dates. "Gold will consolidate at around $350 during the first quarter and then set for rebound as the U.S. stock market could reach its ceiling," he said.
Ted Arnold at Merrill Lynch knocked three dollars off his first quarter estimate noting, "we could easily see it being locked in by the options strangle again."
Jeffrey Christian, managing director of CPM Group, forecast gold at the end of January at $350, end March at $370.
"Gold prices may stay under pressure until the deliveries from the Dutch gold sale are out of the way," he said.
Peter McTeague, an analyst with Boston-based consultants MCM (McCarthy Cristanti Maffei), forecast end-January and end-first quarter prices of $365 and $377 respectively.

"Gold fell to around $355 in first few days of New Year, about one standard deviation from our forecast pivot point for the quarter and...the Dutch central bank gold sale may provide the pyschological support for a bounce back," he said.
